description: Starts a shot plan for you to write: from a short brief it returns a valid skeleton plan (the places to write start with TODO), the layers to write it in, shot-pattern recipes for common kinds of scene, and the first thing to do. The loop is: you write the plan, we check it. We write none of the film and no AI model runs. The brief is sent to us only to build the skeleton, and we don't keep it. Input: brief, a dpl.brief/1 object: title, target_runtime_ms and profile ("film", or "short" for a phone or small-crew shoot), and optionally logline, thesis, characters, places and, for a short, delivery, kit, people and shoot_window. Output: dpl.draft/1, with a skeleton plan that already validates, and next_tool, the tool to call next. Write the first layer into the plan, then follow next_tool. The engine's own wording may name its command line: ignore that and follow next_tool, which names the tool to call next and what to send. A brief with a mistake is refused with each problem and its fix. We don't keep the brief. We log a one-way fingerprint (hash) of it, its size, the tool, the type of client, the result and the time taken. Needs an agent key from a Shoot Plan account. Free, and it does not count toward the account's 3 free projects a month. Plans up to 8 MB and 120 calls a minute (5,000 a day).

brief.description: The brief: a dpl.brief/1 JSON object with title, target_runtime_ms (whole milliseconds) and profile ("film", or "short" for a phone or small-crew shoot); optionally logline, thesis, characters, places and, for a short, delivery, kit, people and shoot_window.
